text: The subject is Hira Shah, who holds account PK**HABB****3642 opened on 23 February 2022. The subject declared an occupation as a Student with a declared monthly income of PKR 30,000 per month. Between 3 April 2026 to 11 April 2026, the account recorded 16 credits totalling PKR 1,018,000 and 4 debits totalling PKR 910,000. The credits consisted of 16 interbank (IBFT) transfers received from 15 distinct senders. An alert was raised by Tazama on 11 April 2026, where Tazama typology MULE-01 scored 360 against an alert threshold of 300. The receipt of funds from 15 distinct senders is indicative of money mule activity. The fact that debits equal to 89% of credits occurred with a median of 1.1 hours between the latest credit and each debit is consistent with suspected money mule activity. The credits in the activity window were 33.9 times the declared monthly income of PKR 30,000 per month for a Student, which is inconsistent with the customer profile and indicative of money mule activity. Two sender banks raised fraud recall requests against inbound transfers to this account, citing scam complaints, which is consistent with suspected money mule activity. The activity, involving 15 distinct senders and credits 33.9 times the declared monthly income of PKR 30,000 per month for a Student, is consistent with suspected money mule activity. PKR 609,000 was sent to QuickPay wallet ***0932 (WLT****0932, Synthetic EMI) in 2 transactions. PKR 301,000 was withdrawn as Cash (ATM) in 2 transactions. There was no match on sanctions, PEP or adverse-media screening on 29 April 2026. Outgoing wallet transfers were placed on hold pending review.
